article.title: Drug case accused dies by suicide in police station in Patiala
article.description: A 29-year-old man arrested in a drugs case allegedly died by suicide in the Nabha city police station on Tuesday.
article.articleTextExcerpt: A 29-year-old man arrested in a drugs case allegedly died by suicide in the Nabha city police station on Tuesday. The deceased was identified as Lachhman Singh, a resident of Sant Nagar. He was arrested on September 27 along with associate Birju while carrying 80 gm of heroin on a motorcycle. A local court on Monday remanded them in two-day police custody. The police officials said around 7 am on Tuesday, Lachhman allegedly hanged himself inside the lock-up toilet using the drawstring of his pyjama. Soon after the incident, a large number of local youths gathered outside the police station and raised slogans against the local police. The situation was brought under control after Patiala SP (Headquarters) Rajesh Chhibber and Nabha DSP Gurinder Singh Bal held talks with the bereaved family. Deceased’s maternal uncle Jaggi Singh and paternal uncle Balvir Singh said the family had viewed the CCTV footage shown by the police and was satisfied that Lachhman had died by suicide. Birju, who was arrested along with him, also reportedly confirmed the sequence of events in the presence of the deceased’s family. However, they expressed resentment over the alleged delay in informing the family.

article.postedBy: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates

article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. The Mumbai Monorail is India’s first and only monorail, running 19.54 km between Chembur and Sant Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle) under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), serving eastern and central Mumbai neighbourhoods that the metro and suburban rail do not reach directly. article.title: Himachal monsoon: State records 13% rainfall deficit in September, Lahaul-Spiti among driest districts
article.description: After witnessing 16 per cent less rainfall in August, Himachal Pradesh continued to experience a weaker monsoon season, with the state recording a 13 per cent rainfall deficit...
article.articleTextExcerpt: After witnessing 16 per cent less rainfall in August, Himachal Pradesh continued to experience a weaker monsoon season, with the state recording a 13 per cent rainfall deficit in September. The state received 103.6 mm of rain against the normal 119.6 mm for the month. According to the State Meteorological Centre, six districts recorded below-normal rainfall, while another six received surplus rain during September. article.articleTextExcerpt: The Police Commissionerate, Ludhiana, has registered a case against the president of the Punjab Dyers Association, along with 250 unidentified persons. The police took action as industrialists and farmers had blocked the national highway near Vardhman Chowk on September 14 over power outages faced by the industry. The police have “secretly” registered a case against the protesters under Section 285 (danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Police Division 7. On September 14, sore over the apathetic attitude of the state government towards the industry, industrialists had blocked the main Ludhiana-Chandigarh National Highway near Vardhman Chowk for about an hour. postedNews.articleTextExcerpt: Assam to Get India’s First Underwater Road-Cum-Rail Tunnel Under Brahmaputra Assam’s ₹18,662-crore Gohpur-Numaligarh corridor includes India’s first underwater road-cum-rail tunnel beneath the Brahmaputra River. Published: Oct 01, 2026, 12:37 IST By: Pawni Mishra Table of Contents Key Facts: Assam India First Underwater Road Cum Rail Tunnel Assam India First Underwater Road Cum Rail Tunnel: What Is Planned? Why the Gohpur-Numaligarh Link Matters Assam India First Underwater Road Cum Rail Tunnel: Areas to Gain Impact on Assam and Northeast Connectivity What Happens Next? Show More Assam is set to get India’s first underwater road-cum-rail tunnel beneath the Brahmaputra River. The project will connect Gohpur on NH-15 with Numaligarh on NH-715 through a new 33.7-km corridor. The Centre has approved a capital cost of about ₹18,662 crore for the project. The new link could also bring more attention to properties in Gohpur and surrounding areas as connectivity improves. Similarly, properties in Numaligarh may see greater interest over time, particularly from buyers tracking major road and rail infrastructure projects.
